title: Privacy Regulation and Barriers to Public Health
near_miss_reason: Every reported column interacts the treatment with a time-invariant state characteristic (c.identification#c.anon, anonymity protection), which is a subgroup-by-treatment interaction, and from Table 1 column 2 onward adds time-varying controls (i.phase eligibility phase, c.t#c.cdc1-cdc4 and c.t#c.tweet barrier/misinformation trends, hydroxy Google-Trends index, lot lottery incentive) and state-specific linear trends (c.t#i.st, Table 1 columns 3-4, all of Table 2). Table 1 column 1 (xtreg vaccine i.t identification c.identification#c.anon, fe r) is the closest to a clean TWFE but still carries the interaction. The treatment is also coded as a switch-OFF: identification equals one from the start of the sample in 32 states and drops to zero in 6 states on 6 distinct days; the event of interest (removal) is what Figure 1 / Table A8 study with relative-time dummies.
eligible_reason: Design qualifies only after recoding the removal of the identification requirement as the switching-on event (6 states, 6 distinct dates, 45 never-switching states); no reported column is free of the identification x anon interaction, and most add state trends and time-varying controls.
design_notes: State-day panel, 51 states x 163 days (Jan 14-Jun 30, 2021), outcome vaccine = daily vaccinations initiated per capita (COVID Act Now); weekly version for Figure 1 and appendix. identification: 26 states always 1, 19 never, 6 switch 1->0 at t = 64, 80, 91, 102, 104, 122 (states 16, 37, 31, 10, 22, 47). anon: time-invariant (43 states protected). Table 1 (Daily Analysis DO File lines 22-34): col 1 xtreg vaccine i.t identification c.identification#c.anon, fe r; col 2 adds i.phase c.t#c.cdc1-4 c.t#c.tweet hydroxy lot; col 3 adds c.t#i.st; col 4 adds c.identification#c.detention. Table 2: subsamples (license==1, sanctuary==0, tweet==0) and phase trends. Figure 1 (weekly file): relative-time dummies ldum4 l3 l2 nrt r1 r2 r3 rdum4 around removal with the full control set and state trends. Random-implementation placebo do-files and a treatment-swapping do-file are included.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Six states remove the identification requirement on six distinct days (t = 64, 80, 91, 102, 104, 122). Under the paper's coding (identification = 1 while the requirement is in force) these are switch-offs; recoded as 'removal' they are six adoption cohorts with 45 never-treated states (26 always-ID, 19 never-ID).
always_treated_note: Under the removal recoding the 19 never-ID states are never-treated controls whose level is absorbed by state FE; under the original coding they are never-treated and the 26 always-ID states are always-treated.

priority_note: Near-miss; a clean TWFE on the removal event is feasible from the shipped data but is not a reported column. Only 6 switching states (cluster-robust inference would be weak; the paper uses heteroskedasticity-robust SEs without clustering).
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Switching dates computed in Python from the daily .dta (6 states, 6 distinct days). Table numbering taken from the do-file comments (Table 1 'Initial Results', Table 2 'Robustness Checks', Figure 1, Tables A7, A8, A12).
